ei.title: Language: A Tool for Mind, Not Its Core
ei.subject: 올림포스전국연합고1_2026

fullPassage: Should we use language to understand mind or mind to understand language? Analytic philosophy historically assumes that language is basic and that mind would make sense if proper use of language was appreciated. Modern cognitive science, however, rightly judges that language is just one aspect of mind of great importance in human beings but not fundamental to all kinds of thinking. Countless species of animals manage to navigate the world, solve problems, and learn without using language, through brain mechanisms that are largely preserved in the minds of humans. There is no reason to assume that language is fundamental to mental operations. Nevertheless, language is enormously important in human life and contributes largely to our ability to cooperate with each other in dealing with the world. Our species homo sapiens has been astonishingly successful, which depended in part on language, first as an effective contributor to collaborative problem solving and much later, as collective memory through written records.

questions.passage: Should we use language to understand mind or mind to understand language? Analytic philosophy historically assumes that language is (A)[secondary / basic] and that mind would make sense if proper use of language was appreciated. Modern cognitive science, however, rightly judges that language is just one aspect of mind of great importance in human beings but not fundamental to all kinds of thinking. Countless species of animals manage to navigate the world, solve problems, and learn without using language, through brain mechanisms that are largely (B)[preserved / lost] in the minds of humans. There is no reason to assume that language is fundamental to mental operations. Nevertheless, language is enormously important in human life and contributes largely to our ability to cooperate with each other in dealing with the world. Our species homo sapiens has been astonishingly (C)[unsuccessful / successful], which depended in part on language, first as an effective contributor to collaborative problem solving and much later, as collective memory through written records.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) basic=기본적인, (B) preserved=보존된, (C) successful=성공적인
det.analysis:
✅ ① basic — preserved — successful: 원문 일치. 분석철학은 언어가 기본적(basic)이라 가정하고, 뇌 기제가 인간 정신에 보존되며(preserved), 호모 사피엔스가 성공적(successful)이었다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ② secondary — preserved — successful: (A) secondary(부차적인)는 basic(기본적인)과 반대
❌ ③ basic — lost — successful: (B) lost(사라진)는 preserved(보존된)의 반의어
❌ ④ basic — preserved — unsuccessful: (C) unsuccessful(실패한)은 successful(성공적인)의 반의어
det.tip: language is basic / mechanisms preserved in minds / astonishingly successful

det.korean: (A) appreciated=제대로 이해된, (B) enormously=엄청나게, (C) collective=집단의
det.analysis:

det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 역할 — (B) 부분(부분적으로): (A)는 맡은 역할, (B)는 'in part(부분적으로)'를 뜻하므로 다의어의 두 의미를 올바르게 연결 ←정답
❌ ② (A) 부분 — (B) 역할: (A)의 part는 play a part에서 역할
❌ ③ (A) 역할 — (B) 부품: (B)의 part는 기계 부품이 아닌 '부분'
❌ ④ (A) 지역 — (B) 역할: (A)는 역할, (B)는 부분
det.tip: part: ① 역할(play a part) ② in part(부분적으로) ③ 부분 ④ (기계) 부품

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "to work together with others in order to achieve something"

det.korean: cooperate=협력하다 (무언가를 이루기 위해 다른 사람들과 함께 일하다)
det.analysis:
❌ ① navigate(길을 찾아가다): 이동으로 정의와 다름
❌ ② preserve(보존하다): 지키는 것으로 정의와 무관
❌ ③ judge(판단하다): 판정으로 정의와 다름
✅ ④ cooperate(협력하다): 무언가를 이루기 위해 함께 일하는 것으로 영영 정의에 정확히 일치 ←정답
det.tip: cooperate = 협력하다. work together with others가 핵심 단서

questions.passage: The success of our species depended in part on language, first as an __________ (effectively) contributor to collaborative problem solving and much later, as collective memory.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 명사 contributor를 수식하는 형용사 effective (부사 effectively → 형용사 effective)
det.analysis: 'an __________ contributor'에서 명사 contributor를 수식하는 형용사가 필요하다. 부사 effectively(효과적으로)를 형용사 effective(효과적인)로 바꾼다. effectively → effective
det.tip: effectively(부사) → effective(형용사). 명사(contributor) 앞에는 형용사

questions.passage: Countless species of animals learn without using language, through brain mechanisms that are largely __________ (preservation) in the minds of humans.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: are + 과거분사 preserved: 수동태 '보존되어 있다'
det.analysis: 'brain mechanisms that are largely __________'에서 be동사 are 뒤에 수동태를 이루는 과거분사가 필요하다. 명사 preservation(보존)을 동사 preserve의 과거분사 preserved로 바꾼다. preservation → preserved
det.tip: be + p.p.(수동태): are largely preserved(대체로 보존되어 있다)

questions.passage: Should we use language to understand mind or mind to understand language? Analytic philosophy historically assumes that language is basic and that mind would make sense if proper use of language was appreciated. Modern cognitive science, however, rightly judges that language is just one aspect of mind of great importance in human beings but __________. Countless species of animals manage to navigate the world, solve problems, and learn without using language, through brain mechanisms that are largely preserved in the minds of humans. There is no reason to assume that language is fundamental to mental operations. Nevertheless, language is enormously important in human life and contributes largely to our ability to cooperate with each other in dealing with the world. Our species homo sapiens has been astonishingly successful, which depended in part on language, first as an effective contributor to collaborative problem solving and much later, as collective memory through written records.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: not fundamental to all kinds of thinking=모든 종류의 사고에 근본적이지는 않은 — 언어는 정신의 중요한 한 측면일 뿐
det.analysis:
❌ ① the only source of all human intelligence(모든 인간 지능의 유일한 원천): 언어가 사고의 전부가 아니라는 논지와 반대
✅ ② not fundamental to all kinds of thinking(모든 사고에 근본적이지는 않은): 언어는 정신의 중요하지만 유일하지 않은 한 측면이라는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ③ impossible for any animal to develop(어떤 동물도 발달시킬 수 없는): 본문의 초점과 다름
❌ ④ far more important than any brain mechanism(어떤 뇌 기제보다 중요한): 동물이 언어 없이 뇌 기제로 사고한다는 맥락과 반대
det.tip: one aspect of mind ... but not fundamental to all kinds of thinking

not fundamental to all kinds of thinking
impossible for any animal to develop

Analytic philosophy historically assumes that language is basic and that mind would make sense if proper use of language was appreciated. Modern cognitive science, however, rightly judges that language is just one aspect of mind of great importance in human beings but not fundamental to all kinds of thinking. Countless species of animals manage to navigate the world, solve problems, and learn without using language, through brain mechanisms that are largely preserved in the minds of humans. There is no reason to assume that language is fundamental to mental operations. Nevertheless, language is enormously important in human life and contributes largely to our ability to __________. Our species homo sapiens has been astonishingly successful, which depended in part on language, first as an effective contributor to collaborative problem solving and much later, as collective memory through written records.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: cooperate with each other in dealing with the world=세상에 대처하는 데 서로 협력하다 — 언어가 기여하는 능력
det.analysis:
❌ ① avoid all forms of social contact(모든 사회적 접촉을 피함): 협력과 반대
❌ ② completely replace our brain mechanisms(뇌 기제를 완전히 대체함): 본문에 없는 내용
✅ ③ cooperate with each other in dealing with the world(세상에 대처하며 서로 협력함): 언어가 서로 협력하는 능력에 크게 기여한다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ stop depending on any written records(문자 기록 의존을 멈춤): 본문과 반대
det.tip: contributes to our ability to cooperate with each other in dealing with the world
